case_title: Sonu v. Sonu Yada V and Another
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304-B, s.498-A; Dowry Prohibition Act s.3, s.4
evidence_type: FIR, medical prescription, phone call records
aggravating_circumstances: Harassment over dowry demands, unnatural death within a year of marriage
neutral_facts: The accused, who was married to the deceased, was alleged to have harassed the deceased over dowry demands. A First Information Report (FIR) was registered by the deceased's brother, alleging that the accused made a phone call demanding additional dowry shortly before the deceased's death. The accused was initially denied bail by the trial court, but the High Court granted bail without providing any reasoning. The accused's medical prescription was submitted, which was claimed to indicate no serious ailment. The Supreme Court overturned the High Court's decision, stating that the bail order lacked proper reasoning and was not justified given the serious allegations of harassment and the unnatural death of the deceased within a year of marriage.
